knowledge.operating_context: git merge conflict resolution across two independent repo clones of nexus-business-os
knowledge.source_locator: nexus-business-os commit 5686e14 (merge) + CURRENT_STATE.md MAIN/FEAT MERGE section
knowledge.statement: Merging feat/unified-system-governance-v0.1 into main found 21 files under .nexus/expert_foundry and related paths that BOTH the Claude Code clone and the Codex/ChatGPT clone had independently authored from the same source package. Assuming either side's whole file is authoritative is wrong in both directions: of the 6 files with real content differences, the correct answer alternated by file (main was right for the rolling-mill dimensions JSON and CURRENT_STATE.md's narrative on this occasion, but that is not a rule -- it was right because it carried the later user-confirmed data, verified by comparing evidence_locator dates and claim content, not by which clone produced it).
knowledge.title: Two independently-maintained git clones silently rebuild the same files differently

payload.observed_outcome: Resolved by diffing each conflicting file's actual content and dating evidence (claim IDs, evidence_locator, narrative dates) rather than picking a side wholesale; verified with the full test suite (814 passed) before finalizing the merge.
payload.validation_plan: Next time this repo shows an add/add conflict between the two clones, diff by content hash first (see next record) and resolve per-file on evidence recency, not clone identity.

knowledge.operating_context: git merge conflict triage on files copied between Windows and this repo
knowledge.source_locator: nexus-business-os merge session 2026-09-14, device_bash diff commands
knowledge.statement: Of 20 files git reported as add/add conflicts during the main/feat merge, 14 were byte-identical content -- the only difference was CRLF (from a Windows-side file copy out of an audit ZIP) vs LF. Diffing with `tr -d '\r'` on both sides before trusting a conflict report separated the 14 false positives from the 6 real ones in seconds, instead of manually reading ~6000 diff lines across 21 files.
knowledge.title: CRLF-vs-LF line endings produce false-positive git add/add conflicts

payload.observed_outcome: Cut real investigation from ~6000 diff lines to 6 files, ~250 real diff lines.
payload.validation_plan: Make content-hash diffing (ignoring line endings) the first step of any future merge-conflict triage in this repo.

knowledge.operating_context: performing a git merge on nexus-business-os through the device-bridge sandbox shell
knowledge.statement: In the Claude device-bridge sandbox (device_bash), git processes can create index.lock/HEAD.lock/objects/*/tmp_obj_* under the bind-mounted nexus-business-os folder but cannot unlink them afterward (EPERM), even though rename works fine. This broke `git worktree add` + `git merge` outright (fatal: Unable to create index.lock: File exists on the very next git call). The reliable workaround: do the merge via plumbing (`git read-tree -m <base> <ours> <theirs>` then resolve conflicts with `git update-index --cacheinfo`, `git write-tree`, `git commit-tree`, `git update-ref`) with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at a scratch path outside the mounted folder (e.g. $HOME/scratch_index) -- that filesystem allows normal unlink.
knowledge.title: Device-bridge sandbox cannot unlink files under the bind-mounted repo folder

payload.observed_outcome: Merge completed and verified (814 tests passed) without ever needing a working-tree checkout of main in the mounted folder.
payload.validation_plan: Default to the plumbing-plus-scratch-index pattern for any future merge/rebase in this repo via device_bash; only try a normal worktree checkout first if this stops reproducing.
